key_insight: A conformal-prediction layer turns neural-operator CFD surrogates into reliability-aware predictors, producing calibrated uncertainty for both vehicle-level drag and spatial surface fields.
engineering_relevance: This helps automotive engineers rank which geometries and surface regions need expensive CFD verification, improving design iteration efficiency without losing reliability.
method: GeoTransolver is used as the main neural-operator surrogate, with Transolver used to assess transfer across architectures.
Drag coefficient uncertainty is calibrated with conformalized quantile regression to produce case-level prediction intervals.
Surface pressure and wall shear stress use point prediction plus residual-scale estimation and residual-normalized conformal calibration for spatially adaptive intervals.
evidence_signal: On the DrivAerML dataset with 90% nominal coverage targets, out-of-fold calibration reduced drag-coverage variability from 10.41 to 3.10 percentage points and cut mean surface-interval width by 22.68% for pressure and 25.35%–27.09% for WSS.
watch_item: The most conservative calibration improves reliability but can widen intervals, so deployment must balance tighter spatial uncertainty estimates against vehicle-level risk tolerance.
paper_title: Multi-Granularity Conformal Prediction for Reliable Neural-Operator Automotive Aerodynamic Surrogates
